newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand says 13 citizens have left Phnom Penh.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand says 13 citizens have left Phnom Penh.

text.p: New Zealand said on Wednesday 13 of its citizens had been evacuated from Cambodia but said there were no immediate plans to organise airlifts for those remaining inside the country. The New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs said its embassy in Bangkok, which covers Cambodia, had confirmed the group left Phnom Penh for Bangkok on Tuesday evening on flights provided by the Thai government.
"There is no current intention to evacuate New Zealanders from Cambodia," the ministry added in a statement.

"Our embassy in Bangkok has been in consultation with the Thais and others about contingency planning for possible evacuation of New Zealanders from Cambodia. We would stress that this is just contingency planning at this stage."
The ministry said it was originally aware of about 60 New Zealanders in Cambodia before Tuesday's evacuation.
It said the security situation in Phnom Penh was reported to be relatively quiet and stable, although still tense. The situation outside Phnom Penh remained uncertain with some factional fighting.

"We are continuing through the Bangkok embassy and other channels to keep a close eye on the situation in Cambodia. Should evacuation become necessary we would coordinate with other countries involved in the situation in Cambodia," the ministry said, adding that telecommunications with Cambodia were now becoming more reliable.
Fighting began in Phnom Penh on Saturday after troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen moved against those supporting First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
